ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated, the lines $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ are the graphs of the functions $y=k_{1}x+b_{1}$ and $y=k_{2}x+b_{2}$, respectively. Based on the graph, what is the solution set of the inequality $k_{1}x+b_{1}>k_{2}x+b_{2}$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} When $x<-2$, $k_{1}x+b_{1}>k_{2}x+b_{2}$,\\
thus the solution set of the inequality $k_{1}x+b_{1}>k_{2}x+b_{2}$ is $x<-2$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $x=\boxed{-2}$.
